page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.large is an entry-tier virtual machine configuration within the shared instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 2 x86_64 vCPUs derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Compute capacity relies on shared core allocation rather than dedicated processor slicing. The configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks bundled local storage, containing zero local disk space, and does not include discrete GPU acceleration. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of shared hardware and low core density. In processor stress tests, the system achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1284.39 and a multi-core score of 1722.27, both placing in the lower percentiles. Geekbench evaluation shows minimal scaling between single-core performance (724.0) and multi-core performance (774.0), consistent with contention or scheduling limits inherent in shared single-core hyper-threaded allocations. Memory bandwidth tests reveal limited throughput for large blocks, measuring 2.01 GB/sec read and 1.99 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB datasets, while PassMark memory scored 582.75.

Application and synthetic throughput metrics follow similar patterns, with static web serving reaching 0.26 GB/sec and Redis SET performance recorded at 1.35 million operations per second. PassMark database operations registered at 528.32. Given the shared vCPU model and modest throughput, the configuration delivers a low-overhead computing profile suited for budget-sensitive deployments that do not require sustained compute or high I/O consistency. Tradeoffs include unpredictable processing bursts, absent local disk volumes, and minimal networking headroom. Workloads best aligned with this profile include non-critical microservices, background utilities, lightweight staging environments, and basic automation tasks.
